briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Croptober Growth: Michigan Brands Expand West as National Psychedelics Pipeline Accelerates
briefs.top: Michigan operators are finding daylight under the 24% wholesale tax — demand is holding, a hometown chain just bought its way into Arizona, and the GOP nominee for governor is campaigning on repeal. Nationally, DEA opened the door wider for medical cannabis registration and Compass Pathways planted a U.S. flag as its psilocybin drug races toward a Q4 filing.

local.text: JARS Cannabis bets big out West — The Michigan-based chain is acquiring Sonoran Roots and its eight Ponderosa dispensaries, a deal that will make JARS the largest dispensary operator in Arizona.
Bloom City Club opens Ypsilanti doors — Ann Arbor's Bloom City Club is celebrating its new Ypsilanti location with a slate of cannabis-themed events running through October.

Demand holds steady despite the 24% tax — Fears that the wholesale tax would crater sales haven't materialized two months in, with licensed operators largely absorbing the cost instead of losing shoppers to the illicit market.
GOP nominee courts industry with repeal pledge — John James has vowed to kill or cut the 24% wholesale tax, and operators including JARS Cannabis executives are backing his campaign with real money.

Regulators clean house, Bay City reinvests tax dollars — State regulators revoked 20 cultivation licenses and fined a mislabeling operator $2 million this week, while Bay City moves to spend $150,000 in cannabis tax revenue to keep a homeless drop-in center open another year.

national.text: DEA opens new path for medical cannabis firms — The Diversion Control Division launched a fresh Form 225 application process so state-licensed medical cannabis manufacturers, distributors and labs can still register for Schedule III status.

Compass Pathways plants a U.S. flag — The psilocybin drugmaker opened its first U.S. office in Jersey City this week, with Breakthrough Therapy-designated COMP360 targeting a completed Q4 2026 NDA filing.
DEA's own data undercuts overdose fears — The agency's 2026 Drugs of Abuse report again found no marijuana overdose deaths, muddying the case rescheduling opponents are trying to build.

Rescheduling hearing paused, not rejected — A DEA judge stayed the Schedule I-to-III proceeding to weigh a new GAO report, but the pause doesn't touch April's order already moving state-licensed medical cannabis to Schedule III.
Psychedelics pipeline widens past psilocybin — Definium reported a second positive Phase 3 trial of LSD for generalized anxiety disorder, adding another compound to the federal fast-track push.
